title: Did New Jersey's 1992 minimum-wage increase reduce fast-food employment? A replication of Card and Krueger (1994)
question: Does a replication of Card and Krueger (1994, American Economic Review) from their public data reproduce the difference-in-differences estimate of the change in full-time-equivalent employment per store in New Jersey relative to eastern Pennsylvania?
brief: Replicate the headline difference-in-differences estimate in Card and Krueger (1994), 'Minimum Wages and Employment: A Case Study of the Fast-Food Industry in New Jersey and Pennsylvania', using the public data at https://davidcard.berkeley.edu/data_sets/njmin.zip (410 stores). Follow the paper's definition of full-time-equivalent employment and its sample rules, reproduce the published comparison, then pre-specify and report at least one robustness check from the later literature.

data.license: Distributed publicly by the author for research use; no explicit licence stated

requirements: Full-time-equivalent employment is defined as in the paper.
Record the replicated headline estimate as a result claim with id `did-fte` and its standard error as `did-fte-se`, and the balanced-sample estimate as `did-fte-balanced`.
The paper reports the published and replicated estimates side by side, with any difference explained.
